title: No Front Lines: A Decision Guide for Companies Caught in Conflict
gist: CSIS report offering a decision guide for corporate boards on risk when companies become targets in conflict, citing Iran's March-April 2026 threats against Gulf data centers; only the abstract is available.

insights.claim: Iran threatened not just military bases but data centers across the Gulf in March and April 2026, illustrating that companies are now on the front lines of war.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Physical and geopolitical risk to Gulf data center assets is real; reassess exposure and insurance.
insights.quote: It chose to threaten not just military bases but data centers across the Gulf.

insights.claim: In an interconnected, just-in-time world companies' missions are unchanged but the nature of war has changed, so boards need a framework to evaluate risk before assisting in a conflict.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Boards should embed conflict-risk evaluation and mitigation planning.

insights.claim: The report offers C-suite questions to identify knowledge gaps, a risk evaluation framework, mitigation strategies and recommendations for the White House on reducing risks to companies caught in conflict.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Signals possible government protections or guidance for firms in conflict zones.

top_entities: International Committee of the Red Cross
